DF 53.16 native symbol-picker historical-figure description
==========================================================

This is a static reconstruction from the two native Windows PE images named
in data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. The adjacent assembly and source tables
are extracted executable source material. No game process was opened, no
desktop interaction occurred, and no generated sample paragraphs were run.

Reader: tools/native_caption_image.py / NativePE, fixed native objdump.exe at
C:/Users/WIN11/AppData/Local/Programs/dfcn-toolchains/w64devkit-2.9.1/w64devkit/bin.
Fixed Python supplied with this workspace was used only to read/extract data.
The optional pefile/capstone modules are absent; this existing reader does not
need them. No dependency installation or alternative toolchain was used.

Reference identity: PE:6a70a6d9:02711000.
Classic identity:   PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.

Actual picker call chain
------------------------

render: reference 0x140200070..0x1402094c4;
        classic   0x140200000..0x140209454.
description dispatch: reference 0x1402126d0..0x14021341c;
                      classic   0x140212660..0x1402133ac.
The render calls this dispatch at multiple category/layout branches. Its
historical-figure render paths include reference call sites 0x140201511 and
0x140205145. Dispatch switches on pane[+0x28]. Figure options 1 and 8 resolve
the hovered index pane[+0x444] through vectors pane[+0x158] or pane[+0x2e0].

At 0x1402127c3 it constructs the default formatting context (0x140072080).
At 0x1402127cd it takes the selected historical figure's id from [+0xe0].
At 0x1402127ed it invokes the full historical-figure description producer:
  history = 0x1424f9cb8
  output  = the initially empty local std::string at [rbp+0x40]
  figure  = the actual selected figure pointer
  id      = figure[+0xe0]
  context = the default context
At 0x140212800 it sends the complete string to 0x1408e7310 for native wrapping
into pane[+0x428], using pane[+0x440] as available width. Render draws those
wrapped rows in yellow (0x6). This is a paragraph, not independent creature,
pronoun, or name labels.

Classic producer call is 0x14021277d, wrap call 0x140212790 -> 0x1408e4b80.
The same producer's other direct caller is the Legends description builder:
reference 0x140b8f0bf, classic 0x140b8c0ff. figure-callers.tsv records both
direct callers, preserving separate picker and Legends ownership.

Producer boundaries and tense
-----------------------------

reference entry / unwind range: 0x140c2b870..0x140c2ced3.
classic entry / unwind range:   0x140c288b0..0x140c29f13.
Equivalent main-producer instructions are reference minus 0x2fc0. This does
not apply to unrelated functions or read-only-data addresses.
Return at reference 0x140c2cea5 is followed by embedded jump tables; objdump's
subsequent data disassembly is not an additional text-producing branch.

Figure fields used by the prose:
  +02 race, +04 caste, +06 sex, +10 birth year, +38 language_name,
  +aa has_name, +c8/+d0 byte flags, +e0 id, +118 links, +130 information.
Information +48 is the curse/animation descriptor, and information +00 holds
the sphere vector. Its values are output in reverse vector order.

The producer tests global mode 0x14189c298 against 3 for every tense-sensitive
clause. Mode 3 uses was, past depictions and the hearsay/myth qualifiers;
other modes use is, current depictions and the present deity/force wording.
The screenshot's is + first-of-kind wording is the current branch of this
same complete producer, not a different hard-coded goblin description.

Complete text-producing branches
--------------------------------

1. Subject (0x140c2b9af..0x140c2b9ed)
   Named figures use historical-figure formatter 0x140b92f10 with default
   context and suppressed extra species noun. Nameless figures use the exact
   literal "This nameless being". Append " is " or " was ".

2. Force identity (0x140c2ba1f..0x140c2bb3e)
   When figure flag bit 3 is set and deity bit 2 is not set:
     subject + is/was + "a force"
   Resolve region through 0x1405c3760 using the figure id. A known region adds:
     current: " which permeates " + formatted region language name
     past:    " which was said to permeate " + that same name.
   Unknown region has no suffix. Then append ".  ".

3. Deity identity (0x140c2bb43..0x140c2bc63)
   Figure flag bit 2 has priority over bit 3 and animation identity:
     subject + is/was + "a deity"
   Iterate entities and find the first entity whose [+0xfc8] vector contains
   this figure id. A known entity adds:
     current: " of " + entity language name at [+0x20]
     past:    " that occurs in the myths of " + that same name.
   No matching entity means no entity suffix. Then append ".  ".

4. Animated identity (0x140c2bc68..0x140c2bd62)
   Selected only when neither deity nor force applies. Information+48 must
   exist and its [+0x144] animation discriminator must not be -1.
   Take its [+0x150] stored identity label. If its [+0x140] original-figure id
   does not resolve, prefix "a "; if it resolves, append the stored label
   directly. In either case add ", animated by unknown forces" + ".  ".
   The label can be a generated personal identity or a complete raw noun,
   status, caste, or supernatural identity; it is not always a person name.

5. Ordinary identity and birth (0x140c2bd67..0x140c2be4d)
   Append "a ". Add "ghostly " only when figure flag bit 7 is set and there
   is no active named curse descriptor [+0x88]. Append caste/race singular
   through 0x140b94ed0 -> 0x140aa3bd0. Invalid race uses "creature".
   Active named curse adds a space plus its stored [+0x90] label.
   If birth year >=1, add " born in " + numeric birth year (0x140b92640 with
   tick=-1), then ".  " and the parentage branches below.
   If birth year <1, no birth clause is emitted here. Continue with the four
   initial/rare-individual branches below, unless the raw's flag bit 8 is set.
   The date helper's seasonal and "a time before time" branches are retained
   in its source assembly but cannot be selected by this caller's year/tick.

6. Parentage (0x140c2be52..0x140c2c4d0)
   Find the first links with virtual type 0 (mother) and 1 (father), taking
   each target id from link[+8]. Subject pronouns use sex 1 -> He, 0 -> She,
   otherwise It; possessives use his/her/its.
   No parent ids emits: "He/She/It is/was of unknown parentage" + ".  ".
   Resolve both parent ids against the historical-figure vector. If neither
   resolves, raw flags 67,68,69 together permit that same unknown-parentage
   sentence; otherwise this parentage clause is omitted.
   With a known parent, ask 0x140bb2f30 for the child's relative rank; the
   caller accepts relation enum 6..44 and uses "child" for other results.
   Emit: He/She/It + " is/was the " + rank + " of " + known parent(s).
   Both known parents are output mother then father, joined by " and ".
   The rank helper's actual 39 labels are in figure-enumerated-text.tsv:
     son:      eldest, second through tenth eldest, son, youngest, only
     daughter: eldest, second through tenth eldest, daughter, only, youngest
     child:    eldest, second through tenth eldest, child, youngest, only.
   Helper enum order differs for only/youngest daughter; the extracted table
   preserves each actual enum instead of inferring it from English order.
   One known parent, raw flags 67,68,69 and the missing counterpart adds:
     ".  The identity of " + his/her/its + " mother/father has been lost to time".
   This sentence has no tense-dependent alternative. Append final ".  ".

7. Initial / rare individuals (0x140c2c4d5..0x140c2c5e9)
   Applicable only to ordinary figures born before year 1 whose race does not
   have raw flag bit 8. The beginning of the function counts same-race figures
   in history[+0x60]: same total = ebx, birth-year>=1 total = edi.
   Append He/She/It + is/was + exactly one of:
     edi>0 and ebx-edi<=1: " the first of " + possessive + " kind"
     edi>0 and ebx-edi>1:  " one of the first of " + possessive + " kind"
     edi==0 and ebx<=1:    " the only one of " + possessive + " kind"
     edi==0 and ebx>1:     " one of the only ones of " + possessive + " kind".
   End with ".  ". This is 4 predicates x 3 paired pronouns x 2 tenses,
   including the exact screenshot sentence.

8. Destiny (0x140c2bf48..0x140c2c663)
   Lookup the figure's nemesis record through 0x140dde080. Require its flag
   bit 2. In mode 3 first append:
     "Although accounts vary, it is universally agreed that "
   Append the figure identity again, is/was, and exactly one predicate:
     nemesis bit 10: "chosen by fate as the vanguard of destiny.  "
     else bit 9:    "possessed of an unusual destiny.  "
     otherwise:     "guided by forces unknown.  ".
   No eligible nemesis means no destiny sentence. This may follow any identity
   branch; it is not restricted to the initial/rare-individual paragraph.

9. Deity form (0x140c2c669..0x140c2ca39)
   Only figure flag bit 2. Repeat the figure identity and append:
     current: " most often takes the form of a "
     past:    " was most often depicted as a ".
   Optional prefixes occur in exactly this native order, independently:
     flag bit 4 -> "skeletal ", bit 5 -> "rotting ", bit 7 -> "ghostly ".
   Resolve caste singular [+0x20] and fall back to race singular [+0x20].
   Raw flag bit 66 and a caste name that is empty or identical to the race
   noun permits sex 0 -> "female ", sex 1 -> "male ", other -> no sex prefix.
   These prefix and caste combinations are grammar, not a finite race list.
   Keep this sentence open for optional sphere association below.

10. Generated raw description (0x140c2ca3e..0x140c2ccee)
    For a non-deity, valid race+caste and any caste flag bit 132,134,143,131,
    append the complete caste DESCRIPTION string at [+0x220], then "  ".
    This covers procedurally generated creature and supernatural descriptions,
    rather than another biography literal. The string content is raw data and
    follows the existing complete physical-description grammar.

11. Sphere association (0x140c2ccee..0x140c2ce83)
    Nonempty information[+0x00] sphere vector:
      after a deity form: " and" + is/was + "associated with " + domains
      otherwise: repeat identity + is/was + "associated with " + domains.
    Iterate domain ids last-to-first. Use ", " between the earlier values and
    " and " before the last value. Each uses 0x140756500, which optionally
    prefixes "the " and delegates to 0x140756690 for enum values 0..129.
    figure-enumerated-text.tsv preserves all 130 complete displayed domain
    noun forms per image, including those article choices and addresses.
    Invalid sphere enum assigns no label. The data table is a source enum
    inventory, not a list of hypothetical generated biographies.
    Close the deity form / association sentence with ".  ". With no domains,
    still close an open deity-form sentence. No domains and no deity form
    means no additional text.

Dynamic name and raw fields
---------------------------

figure-helper-functions.tsv maps each reference/classic helper entry. Their
complete assemblies and RIP-literal sources accompany the main producer:
  historical-figure identities 0x140b92f10 / 0x140b8ff50
  language names              0x140a946e0 / 0x140a91760
  caste/race noun              0x140aa3bd0 / 0x140aa0c50
  creature noun wrapper        0x140b94ed0 / 0x140b91f10
  date                        0x140b92640 / 0x140b8f680
  subject pronoun             0x140aa4730 / 0x140aa17b0
  possessive pronoun          0x140aa4850 / 0x140aa18d0
  child-rank label            0x14075a580 / 0x140757fa0
  child-order discriminator   0x140bb2f30 / 0x140baff70
  domain + article            0x140756500 / 0x140753f20
  domain noun                 0x140756690 / 0x1407540b0.

Both identity contexts passed from this picker are default contexts, excluding
interrogation-only/interrogator/self-reference/link-markup cases. The full
helper assemblies retain those other caller branches without classifying them
as picker prose. Native names retain first/nickname/language word fields; raw
race/caste and curse labels are dynamic data, not extra hard-coded sentences.
No flattening of those fields into screenshot-specific person/race lists is
needed to represent all possible descriptions.

Existing full-paragraph translation consumers
---------------------------------------------

The symbol footer pipeline in src/dfcn.cpp calls the complete paragraph entry
translate_symbol_picker_description in src/symbol_picker_descriptions.inc.
That entry prioritizes exact_literal_translation, an item paragraph whose
opening noun resolves as a whole, translate_instrument_description for the
complete RAW field, translate_symbol_description_source for image prose, and
translate_legends_text(source, false, false). It then handles the finite native
site/entity descriptions through scoped templates and shared typed fields.
The historical description grammar is the h namespace, separate
from word matching. The latter consumes every source clause and requires the
whole paragraph to resolve; individual translated goblin/pronoun words do not
represent successful paragraph translation.

The existing data/runtime/local-overrides.tsv biography entries include:
  identity/deity/force current and past: approximately lines 7338..7393
  first-of-kind / one-of-first: 7527..7532 and 7813..7818
  numeric birth: 7716..7728
  two-parent rank templates + 39 rank terms: 7736..7779
  nameless/deity form + domains/force hearsay: 7792..7810
  one-parent/unknown/lost parent: 7832..7846
  animated identities: 7850..7865
  all three destiny predicates + past qualifier: 7869..7881.
The rows around 7527 and 7389 cover all remaining initial/rare combinations.
Generic named creature clauses also handle a deity or force without a known
entity/region, using the scoped creature/deity/force vocabulary.

translate_legends_actor handles the nameless literal, generated names, native
nicknames and typed creature identities. translate_legends_term and its htv
description grammar resolve skeletal/rotting/ghostly and gender/caste forms;
the existing creature and raw-description vocabularies own dynamic species.
translate_deity_spheres strips native "the " per element and uses the existing
sphere namespace, keeping every listed domain and its order.

Manual source reading did not expose a finite biography production requiring
a new dictionary entry. The screenshot's whole current biography, including
"She is one of the first of her kind.", already has the full relevant grammar.
The renderer's footer-region ownership must deliver the complete source to
that grammar; a tail FPS row outside the pane is not the hovered biography.
This source reconstruction does not claim an observed final game display.

Final source-to-consumer correspondence
--------------------------------------

The following correspondence is from the actual instruction/literal sources
above and manual reading of the final source. It records translation ownership,
not executed paragraphs, assertions, a test result or a game-display observation.
Addresses below are reference VAs; paired classic addresses remain in the
adjacent extracted source files. TSV line references identify the current
source rows, not a promise that later edits cannot move them.

Entry and typed captures:
  src/symbol_picker_descriptions.inc:4 dispatches the complete original footer;
  its biography handoff is translate_legends_text(source, false, false).
  src/legends_detail.inc:900 owns that complete h-namespace paragraph. Capture
  dispatch at :971/:972/:1012/:1018 sends actual figure, place, descriptor and
  sphere fields respectively to translate_legends_actor, translate_legends_name,
  translate_legends_term and translate_deity_spheres. The paragraph fails as a
  whole if a source clause remains unconsumed; it does not declare individual
  translated words a successful biography.

  0x140c2b9af..0x140c2b9ed, named/nameless subject:
    The literal "This nameless being" is local-overrides.tsv:7802. The explicit
    special case in src/legends_detail.inc:769 translate_legends_actor resolves
    it inside {n}; native personal names and authored nicknames use that same
    actor's typed name path. No placeholder name is invented for this branch.

  0x140c2ba1f..0x140c2bb3e, force:
    "a force" without a region is the ordinary {n} is/was a {s}. production,
    with the typed creature-kind term force in src/creature_vocabulary.inc:65.
    Known region current "which permeates" has full rules at
    local-overrides.tsv:7384..7387. Actual past "which was said to permeate"
    has separate full rules at :7811..7812. Region remains a {p} name field.

  0x140c2bb43..0x140c2bc63, deity identity:
    Bare "a deity" uses the same ordinary identity templates and the typed
    deity kind (src/creature_vocabulary.inc:38). Current "a deity of" is
    local-overrides.tsv:7379..7380; past "a deity that occurs in the myths of"
    is :7356..7357. Those latter native strings have a separate punctuation
    append; the h namespace also has the complete "." literal, so the full
    sentence and its next clause remain consumable.

  0x140c2bc68..0x140c2bd62, animation:
    Actual suffix ", animated by unknown forces" is owned by
    local-overrides.tsv:7860..7875. These include is/was, both article-bearing
    {s} and article-free {s}, and the separate {n} animated identity. The
    original-figure-id discriminator therefore does not force every stored
    +150 label through a personal-name parser. Typed species/status labels
    reuse src/creature_descriptors.inc:36 and the shared generated vocabulary.

  0x140c2bd67..0x140c2be4d, ordinary identity and numeric birth:
    {n} is/was a/an {s}. is local-overrides.tsv:7351..7354 and :7370..7373.
    The caller's year>=1, tick=-1 "born in" fields are the numeric productions
    at :7726..7729 and :7735..7738. "ghostly" and an active named curse are
    part of the complete {s}; shared species grammar consumes resurrection
    prefixes, caste names and species+display-name/status suffixes. The
    invalid-race noun "creature" has a typed kind (:33), not a guessed name.
    The helper's other time formats cannot be selected by this call.

  0x140c2be52..0x140c2c4d0, parentage:
    All 39 labels actually selected from relation enum 6..44 are present as
    h terms, local-overrides.tsv:7754..7789 plus :7804..7806 for bare
    child/son/daughter. Mother then father, their exact " and " connector,
    and all He/She/It x is/was combinations use the two-parent productions
    :7746..7751. The one-known-parent productions are :7842..7847. The six
    "of unknown parentage" sentences are :7848..7853. The three possessive
    "The identity of ... has been lost to time" templates are :7854..7856,
    with mother/father scoped nouns at :7562..7563. Native omitted-parentage
    cases emit no clause; they are not missing visible text.

  0x140c2c4d5..0x140c2c5e9, initial/rare individuals:
    The four exact predicates are "the first of", "one of the first of",
    "the only one of" and "one of the only ones of". Every paired sex pronoun
    and every tense is represented: :7823..7828, :7537..7542,
    :7364..7369 and :7398..7403. This is the native 24-sentence finite family,
    including "She is one of the first of her kind." at :7541.

  0x140c2bf48..0x140c2c663, destiny:
    All three actual stems, "chosen by fate as the vanguard of destiny",
    "possessed of an unusual destiny" and "guided by forces unknown", have
    complete named/nameless is/was rules at :7879..7890. The mode-3 qualifier
    "Although accounts vary, it is universally agreed that" is its own h
    literal at :7891, followed by the same typed full destiny clause.

  0x140c2c669..0x140c2ca39, deity form:
    Current "most often takes the form of a" with/without associated spheres
    is :7388..7391; actual past "was most often depicted as a" full variants
    are :7815..7817 (also :7361..7363 for linked clause boundaries). The
    skeletal/rotting/ghostly prefixes are independent recursive
    creature-status rows in data/runtime/legends-creature-descriptions.tsv.
    src/legends_detail.inc:450 recursively consumes the complete form before
    :393 handles female/male+species. All three native prefix flags therefore
    retain their order and can coexist; no species-by-species list is needed.

  0x140c2ccee..0x140c2ce83, sphere association:
    Independent is/was associated-with clauses and the joined form clauses
    are local-overrides.tsv:7358..7360, :7392..7394, :7388..7389 and
    :7815..7816. All 130 actual labels in figure-enumerated-text.tsv have
    their sphere senses at :1746..1875, flags r. src/dfcn.cpp:11680 handles
    native "the" labels and complete comma/and list separators, preserving
    the actual reverse-vector order. These noun senses do not use global
    homonymous UI labels or phonetic proper-name fallback.

  0x140c2ca3e..0x140c2ccee, appended caste DESCRIPTION:
    This branch copies a complete +220 string; it creates no new fixed
    English sentence in the biography producer. Static whole RAW descriptions
    go through existing full literals; generated physical/behavior paragraphs
    use data/runtime/legends-creature-descriptions.tsv (complete clause,
    recursive description, color, anatomy and origin fields). The fallback
    at src/legends_detail.inc:1081 consumes complete original sentences through
    exact literals or the existing compositor. The byte string is never
    interpreted as a person's name and an unsupported sentence cannot erase
    the remaining source or silently count as a complete translation.

No additional finite, text-producing branch in this biography producer was
identified without a corresponding complete rule and typed capture consumer.
The finite-branch finding is about this extracted native producer. Runtime
names, custom RAW labels and stored DESCRIPTION contents are separate data
fields; merely forwarding those fields does not prove translation of arbitrary
new user-added English. This distinction does not remove any emitted field
from the footer's complete-source translation path.
